summary: Elaborate 4-ADR + kernel/app machinery for a pipeline that has zero changesets in flight; the design exhibits speculative state machines, double-bookkeeping by its own admission, and a state-enum that the prose miscounts and the code special-cases.

findings.issue: ADR prose declares 'CLOSED ENUM of 9 states' and totals '9 advancing + 3 terminal-fail = 12 closed values', but the table has rows 0..=9 (10 rows) and the kernel ships 13 variants. The kernel comment at crates/oya-foundry-vcs-changeset-state-kernel/src/lib.rs:40-42 explicitly calls out the miscount: 'the ADR prose 9 advancing miscount is resolved here by counting the table rows literally'. Naming-that-lies + ADR-vs-code drift on day 1 of a Proposed ADR.
findings.remediation: Fix the ADR prose to say '10 advancing + 3 terminal-fail = 13 closed values'. Delete the apologetic kernel comment. The ADR is the contract; rewrite it before merge instead of papering over with an in-code disclaimer.

findings.issue: Produced is double-classified: is_terminal() returns true for Produced AND advancing_ordinal() returns Some(9). The validator (lines 301-323) special-cases this with a nested 'if terminal { if let Some(ord)=advancing_ordinal { ... advancing check ... } continue; }'. This is the canonical 'special cases that could be deleted by reshaping the data' anti-pattern. Either Produced is on the advancing axis (terminal-success), or it's a terminal-fail twin — not both.
findings.remediation: Split the enum: AdvancingState (10 variants, ordinal-comparable) + TerminalState (Produced, Abandoned, Rejected, CostExhausted). The log row's to_state becomes Either<Advancing, Terminal>. Validator collapses to one ordinal-monotonic check on Advancing + at-most-one Terminal. Drops the special-case branch entirely.

findings.issue: control-plane-before-scale: 13-state enum + monotonicity validator + closed-enum lane + dedup-key + 4 Proposed ADRs + 5 fitness lanes + projected-merge-state simulation + 4-stage canary controller — and the canonical event log is literally {"events": []}. Zero real changesets have ever traversed this. Five separate ADRs (0110/0111/0112/0113/0114) all status: Proposed land in one PR with no exercised use case.
findings.remediation: Land ADR-0110 + the kernel + the validator + the lane. Postpone ADR-0111/0112/0113/0114 until at least one real changeset has gone opened -> produced and exposed which abstractions earn their keep. Trim 'Wave B/C/D' boilerplate sections that describe lanes that don't exist.

findings.issue: The ADR explicitly admits double-bookkeeping: 'IP-006 admission emits BOTH a tick_log row (queue-internal) AND a changeset-event-log row (pipeline-spanning)'. F1 anti-pattern list literally names 'double-bookkeeping-across-artifacts'. 'A future ADR may unify the two; for now they coexist' is the exact promise that calcifies into permanent duplicate state.
findings.remediation: Decide one writer NOW. Either (a) tick_log is a projection of changeset-event-log via a query, or (b) tick_log is retired and IP-006 emits only changeset-event-log. Don't ship coexistence.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled base64 encoder (30 lines) + hand-rolled proleptic-Gregorian civil-from-days RFC3339 formatter (~50 lines incl. epoch_day_to_ymd). Justified as 'no chrono/time dep so the app stays dep-thin' — but serde_json IS already a dep, base64 is in workspace via other crates, and the timestamp is only used as a string inside dedup_key (no parsing required). Reinventing wheels for an aesthetic.
findings.remediation: Either pull `time` (or even chrono) into workspace deps, or stop pretending the dedup_key needs RFC3339 — a UNIX-epoch nanosecond u128 .to_string() is monotonic, deterministic, and one line. Delete epoch_day_to_ymd + base64_encode.

findings.issue: is_success(&ExitCode) compares `format!("{exit:?}")` against `format!("{:?}", ExitCode::SUCCESS)`. This is a stable-API end-run via Debug formatting on a stdlib type whose Debug impl is explicitly NOT a stable API. Will silently misbehave (always-false) on any Rust release that changes ExitCode's Debug shape, e.g. from 'ExitCode(unix_exit_status(0))' to 'ExitCode(0)'. The verify dispatcher should return a Result<(), ExitCode> or an i32, not a non-introspectable ExitCode.
findings.remediation: Refactor verify::run to return ExitStatus or Result<(), i32>. Convert to ExitCode only at the outermost main()/dispatch. Delete is_success() and the Debug-string comparison.

findings.issue: recover_state_from_ordinal has a saturating `_ => Produced` fallback comment-justified as 'unreachable on a well-typed input'. If unreachable, the right shape is to return Result, not fabricate a wrong-but-plausible state. Currently a buggy upstream that calls with ordinal 99 silently reports 'BackwardsTransition from Produced to X' — a misleading error pinning blame on Produced.
findings.remediation: Carry the from_state through the validator (event.from_state.unwrap_or(...)) only when it's actually Some; otherwise emit a distinct error variant 'MissingFromState' rather than fabricate. Removes the dishonest saturating fallback.

findings.issue: Emergency-rewind writes a 'canary-emergency-rewind' event into changeset-event-log on the original changeset. But ADR-0110 §Open Question 3 commits to: 'a revert is a NEW changeset, not a state regression. Monotonicity is preserved.' If the original changeset already reached `produced` (ordinal 9), there is no advancing state for the rewind row to occupy without violating ADR-0110's invariant — and 'canary-emergency-rewind' isn't in the closed 13-value enum at all. Two ADRs landed in the same PR contradict each other on day 1.
findings.remediation: Pick one model. Either (a) extend the closed enum with a new state and update ADR-0110, or (b) make emergency-rewind open a NEW changeset (consistent with ADR-0110 OQ3) and write the rewind event on THAT changeset's log. Don't ship contradiction.

findings.issue: from_wire does linear scan over Self::ALL recomputing as_wire() per probe. With 13 entries the perf is irrelevant, but a `match value { "opened" => Some(Self::Opened), ... }` is cleaner, faster, and lets the compiler verify exhaustiveness against the same closed-enum invariant the ADR is selling.
findings.remediation: Replace with explicit match. Saves a closure, drops a method indirection, and gives the closed-enum guarantee structurally instead of by-construction.

findings.issue: evidence is BTreeMap<String, String>. ADR-0110's example shows numeric pr_number: 4 and structured cost_budget_remaining: {...}. The 'free-form' justification + the ADR's own enumeration of 4 specific fields = stringly-typed pseudo-schema. Every consumer re-parses, type info evaporates at the boundary.
findings.remediation: Either model evidence as a typed enum per emitter (PrEvent { pr_number: u64, head_sha: String, ... }), OR if truly free-form use BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>. Current shape is the worst of both worlds.

findings.issue: Half-built control plane: STUB_USD/STUB_TOKENS/STUB_INVOCATIONS are stamped on every append; the kernel's CostBudget::is_exhausted() check is wired up but no decrement logic exists. The 'enforcement' lane will green-light forever until wave-B writes the decrementer. Worse, every appended row carries the same constant budget — so the JSON log gets noisier without conveying signal.
findings.remediation: Either (a) make cost_budget_remaining Optional in the kernel + omit from wave-A rows (don't fake data), or (b) bring the decrementer in this PR. Stamping constant '100.0 / 10M / 100' in every row is signal pollution.

findings.issue: `oya vcs override --to-state <reviewed|rejected|abandoned>` accepts terminal-fail values but the ADR doesn't state which transitions an override may legally write. With ADR-0110's MultipleTerminalStates rule, an override-to-rejected on an already-produced changeset is silently rejected by the validator — the override CLI returns success, the underlying append fails. Implicit policy = future bug.
findings.remediation: Add explicit override-transition table to ADR-0113 (e.g., override-to-reviewed only allowed from {ci_passed}, override-to-rejected only allowed from non-terminal advancing states). Make the CLI surface the validator's rejection rather than swallow it.

findings.issue: HARNESS_SIDECAR_PREFIXES (.omc/.omx/.grit/target/) is a bandaid: hook activity races the working-tree clean-check, so the clean-check learns to ignore those paths. Naming-that-lies: 'HARNESS_SIDECAR' admits these are sidecars, but the sanctioned-primitives doctrine in CLAUDE.md says 'no external agent-coordination tooling remains in repo' — so the right fix is hooks-don't-race, not allowlist their droppings. Solving the symptom, not the cause.
findings.remediation: Either (a) make hooks atomic (write to .tmp + rename, OR don't write during oya submit), or (b) gitignore .omc/state/ entirely so it never appears in `git status --porcelain`. The hardcoded prefix list is debt that grows with every new harness.
